title: Propeller pitch system -- blade-pitch position topology (L2: branches + the linear-rotary coupling)

provenance.structure_source: dispatch/docs/strategy/HANDOFF_20260831_tolstack_dag_strategy.md (locked brief), locked decision 1, level L2 -- Jeff's own description of the mechanism: 'VP actuator -> pitch plate connection; branch 1 -> gas spring (or hydraulic brake per design concept); branch 2 -> pitch plate -> pitch links -> pitch arms -> blade roots; from blade roots a further branch -> ring gear (cyclic-only)'. The graph below is that sentence, grounded back to the hub so the parallel paths are actually parallel. Cite the brief for the structure; it is Jeff's description of his own mechanism, not a reading of a drawing.
provenance.values_source: docs/tolerance_stacks/WORKSHEET_end_stop_graft.md, the structured read of data/inbox/tolerance_stacks/260825_End_Stop_JC.xlsx (handoff endstop_graft_workorder, 2026-08-25). Every band that has a source is a `workbook` citation to a cell of that sheet, `untraced` -- which is the whole sheet's status: that worksheet's count is 0 traced, 0 inferred, 43 untraced of 43 element instances, and this document closes none of those gaps.
provenance.values_are_placeholders: THE TOPOLOGY IS THE DELIVERABLE; THE VALUES ARE NOT. Bands with no workbook row carry `kind: "assumed"` and say so in their note. Even the sourced ones are one author's provisional workbook, two of which (rows 26 and 57) carry the author's own comment that the number needs correcting. Nothing here is fit to size a part.
provenance.variation_only: EVERY dimension in this document has `nominal: 0.0`. These are not lengths -- they are tolerance bands about an unstated nominal, because that is what the source sheet holds: a column of total tolerance widths, not dimensions (its own row 72 comment: 'note this is total range (divide by 2 for +/-)'). So min/max are -w/2 and +w/2 for a stated total width w, and a study's `nominal` total is 0 by construction while its worst-case and RSS bands are the real result. Mixing a nominal-carrying dimension into this topology would make the nominal column read as a position sum when it is not one; if real nominal lengths arrive, they arrive for ALL of these edges at once, or in a separate topology.
provenance.geometry_not_in_the_bands: Nominal geometry that IS known -- pitch arm radius 50 mm, blade root radius 32 mm, pitch link length 109.4 mm at a 77 deg link angle, gas-spring bushing separation 34.7 mm -- is carried in `properties` on the edge or transform it belongs to, never in a `dimension`. It is context for a transform, not a term in a variation sum.

properties.how_the_source_obtained_it: a constant typed into the source sheet, described there as CAD-sourced; NOT derived from the radii above, which are recorded here because they are the coupling's geometry and because the tangential transform below is derived from them

source_ref.note: PLACEHOLDER RATIO, and doubly so. (1) The cell is an unsourced CAD-derived constant in a workbook that traces nothing. (2) Its own comment reads 'full sweep average' while it sits in the column headed 'pitch -5deg (worst)', and row 9's comment says 'at 40deg pitch' -- three different operating conditions named around one number. WORKSHEET_end_stop_graft.md flags this as F1 and says to ask Jeff before trusting the D column's precise value at -5 deg. Do not quote this ratio as a result.

transforms.note: THE one non-trivial transform this level of the model requires: vertical displacement of the pitch plate converted into blade pitch angle at the pitch arm. Applied by a study to every vertical contributor upstream of the pitch arm, which is exactly what the source sheet's D column does.

source_ref.note: PLACEHOLDER RATIO. The source sheet's second sensitivity column, described as the full-sweep-average motion ratio and explicitly not a literal average over angle (WORKSHEET_end_stop_graft.md section 1).

transforms.note: The same coupling at the other operating condition. Its reason for existing in the schema is structural: one topology, two transform sets, selected per study -- which is why a study carries a `transforms` map at all.

source_ref.note: PLACEHOLDER RATIO, inheriting every caveat on D10 because it is D10 x B11. B11 = 50/32 with the sheet's own comment 'uses ratio of pitch arm to blade root radius'; that lever ratio IS the linear-rotary coupling's geometry at the pitch arm, taken at the blade-root radius instead of the pitch-plate one.

transforms.note: The same pitch-arm coupling, for a contributor that acts tangentially at the blade root rather than vertically at the pitch plate. This is the only edge in the repo that declares a non-identity transform as its default, and it does so because the linear-rotary conversion here is the geometry of the pitch arm itself, not a choice of output quantity: a displacement across this edge IS an angle at the blade. notes: This is the L2 deliverable: the pitch system's STRUCTURE, with four branch points, three grounded loops (pitch links, gas spring, ring gear), one gap edge, and the one linear-rotary coupling the brief requires. It is not an analysis and none of its numbers should be quoted. Two thirds of the bands are workbook cells from a sheet that traces nothing; the rest are marked `assumed`.

The three loops are the whole reason the not-a-solver rule is written down. hub -> actuator -> pitch plate -> pitch links -> pitch arm -> blade root -> hub, hub -> ... -> pitch plate -> gas spring -> gas-spring mount -> tangential link mount -> hub, and blade root -> ring gear -> hub are three statically redundant paths from the same source to the same ground. Which one carries the load is a mechanics question. A study picks one; nothing in the code will pick for you, and `Topology.branch_nodes()` exists to show a study author where the choices are (here: the hub A datum, the hub top deck, the pitch plate connection, and the pitch-arm/blade-root clocking).

TRANSFORM COVERAGE, deliberately incomplete. The source sheet has THREE sensitivity columns and this document declares two of the three coupling pairs: the vertical one (its D10/F10) and the blade-root tangential one (D11/F11). Its third -- the pitch-plate tangential sensitivity (D12/F12 = D10 x K12) -- is NOT declared, because K12 is a finite-difference linearisation of the pitch link's own geometry evaluated once at the nominal 77 deg link angle, and copying the resulting constant here would present a derivation as a datum. The gas-spring and tangential rows therefore have no honest blade-angle sensitivity in this document, and `study_gas_spring_branch_to_hub` is a millimetre study for that reason. Adding the third pair means either recording the linearisation as a transform `properties` payload with a reader for it, or getting the sensitivity from Jeff.

LOAD CASES have no home in v0, and the ring-gear branch is where that bites: per the brief it participates cyclically and follows along for pure collective, so a collective study should exclude it and a cyclic study should not. Today that distinction lives in which edges a human puts in `selection`, which works and is unlabelled. If it needs a name, a study-level `configuration` block (the stack schema already has one on checks) is the cheap shape.

WHAT THIS TOPOLOGY CANNOT REPRODUCE, stated so nobody assumes it can. The source sheet applies a diameter-MMC weighting factor built from the two blade-root bearing radii to three of its rows (17, 19, 20), and derives its largest single contributor (row 68, gas-spring bushing tipping backlash, 0.72 deg) from a radial clearance and two lever arms. Neither is expressible with one ratio per edge. That is a schema finding, not an oversight: it says the next transform kind is a weight computed from `properties`, and it says the brief's 'the pitch-system L2 case should be able to represent that workbook's structure' is true of the structure and not yet true of the arithmetic.

The full 43-row import of that workbook is deliberately NOT done. The brief calls it 'a sanity check of the schema, not a required import', and it has served as one: the four findings above all came out of trying. What is here is the brief's named structure carrying a representative band per edge.
